## Detailed entries

### Morristown

- **Type:** Town
- **Recorded status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-08-31 (Select Board and Village Board of Trustees joint unanimous vote, dated interim zoning bylaw)
- **Normalized date:** `2026-08-31` (exact)
- **Duration:** Two years from adoption, as an interim zoning bylaw
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center, general
- **Moratorium ID:** `vt-morristown-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Interim zoning bylaw adopted unanimously by the Morristown Select Board and Village of Morrisville Board of Trustees, dated 2026-08-31, following a selectboard proposal and two public hearings in August 2026
- **What prompted it:** Town bylaws are silent on data centers and 'high-impact uses'; board wants time for the planning commission to study electric-grid, water, noise, and hazardous-waste impacts before any application is filed, prompted in part by community reaction to a separate large industrial-park/quarry proposal
- **Affected projects:** None named; officials and residents confirmed no data center has been proposed in Morristown and few parcels are large enough to host one, but the board called the moratorium precautionary.
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-09-23. The interim zoning bylaw (dated 2026-08-31) blocks consideration of applications for data centers and other defined 'high-impact uses' -- facilities that consume 10+ megawatts of power from any source, use 57,600+ gallons of water per day, discharge hazardous waste, add more than 10 acres of impervious surface, or emit more than 70 decibels of persistent noise -- for two years, with an exemption for small data centers necessary for the administrative/operational support of an existing business, hospital, school, municipal service, or residence. Intended to give the planning commission time to draft permanent zoning addressing such uses; runs through approximately 2028-08-31.
- **Outcome:** Adopted unanimously by the Select Board and Village Board of Trustees on 2026-08-31 after a public hearing with dozens of residents, most supportive; Morristown is the third Vermont community (after Royalton's permanent five-year ban and South Burlington's zoning amendment) to restrict data centers.

### H.727 (2025-2026)

- **Policy ID:** `vt-h-727-2025-2026`
- **Sponsor / party:** Rep. Laura Sibilia; I (Sibilia is an Independent in the Vermont House per VT General Assembly member roster)
- **Recorded status:** Passed House and Senate, vetoed by Governor Scott, veto sustained on House reconsideration vote (Yeas 83, Nays 52; 90 Yeas of 135 needed to override) -- 2026-05-29; bill did not become law
- **Provisions:** Would create the Vermont Sustainable Data Centers Act for facilities using or able to use 20 MW or more; requires Public Utility Commission approval of large load service equity contracts, cost allocation to protect other ratepayers, collateral for stranded-cost risk, demand management provisions, energy efficiency consultation, quarterly water and energy reporting, Act 250 jurisdiction for data center construction, closed-loop cooling preference, water withdrawal permits, PFAS monitoring, and annual Department of Public Service reporting.
- **Mechanism / scope:** utility_large_load_restriction; utility_grid
- **Legal effect:** failed
- **Effective date:** —
- **End condition and limitations:** —
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://legislature.vermont.gov/bill/status/2026/H.727>)

### S.205 (2025-2026)

- **Policy ID:** `vt-s-205-2025-2026`
- **Sponsor / party:** Sen. Rebecca White; Sens. Seth Bongartz, Ruth Hardy, Joseph Major, Tanya Vyhovsky; D (White, Bongartz, Hardy, Major); P/D (Vyhovsky caucuses with Vermont Progressive Party / Democratic fusion)
- **Recorded status:** Died at sine die adjournment of the 2025–2026 biennium on 2026-05-29: the official bill page lists its last recorded legislative action as the 2026-01-06 Senate Finance referral and contains no act information. The page lists a 2026-02-18 Finance committee meeting; whether a committee vote occurred was not independently established.
- **Provisions:** Would prohibit operation, site preparation, or construction of an AI data center before 2030-07-01; defines AI data center as a facility requiring more than 100 MW of new load for AI inference, training, simulation, or synthetic data generation; requires Public Utility Commission investigation and report by 2027-01-15.
- **Mechanism / scope:** statewide_moratorium; statewide
- **Legal effect:** failed
- **Effective date:** —
- **End condition and limitations:** —
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://legislature.vermont.gov/bill/status/2026/S.205>)
